title: Uterus ultrasound after birth
what: This ultrasound shows how the uterus is shrinking back after birth and whether anything is left inside.
why: Before going home from the maternity hospital, after a C-section, or if pain, fever, or heavy bleeding bother you after birth.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; the result is given right away
tell_doctor: How you gave birth: vaginally or by C-section
How many days ago you gave birth
What your bleeding is like: how much, what color, and if it smells
If you have a fever or pain

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: For an ultrasound through the belly, you may be asked to fill your bladder a little. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes and a spare pad.

steps: You lie on the exam table
The doctor looks at the uterus with a probe on your belly
Sometimes a probe inside the vagina is also used
The doctor measures the uterus and checks inside it
The gel is wiped off, and you are told the result
feel: After a C-section, pressure from the probe near the scar can be unpleasant
after: You are told the result right away
Bleeding after birth usually lasts up to 6 weeks and slowly gets lighter
If something is found, the doctor will tell you what to do next
red_flags: Heavy bleeding: a pad is fully soaked within an hour
Bad-smelling discharge or severe lower belly pain

faq.q: Can I have an ultrasound while breastfeeding?
faq.a: Yes. Ultrasound does not affect breastfeeding.

faq.q: Why an ultrasound if I feel fine?
faq.a: Sometimes problems show up before you notice symptoms. Your doctor decides if you need it.

reminders.text: Uterus ultrasound after birth tomorrow. Bring your hospital discharge summary and a pad.
